chapter: Learning from players; Jonah Jones lessons
title: Jonah Jones loses his lip: how Maxwell found out
summary: Maxwell overhears Jonah in a practice studio huffing; Jonah has new caps.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: We were talking, Jimmy, about your teaching. I know you were talking about these young people who come to you and some of them are very anxious, because I have that same

problem, some young people come to me and say, 'look, I want you to teach me a song.' I say, well, I'm not going to teach you a song, I'll teach you to play conserva-tive bass and you conservative trumpet. And you mentioned how you have to straighten them out.

And I also know that you've been able to straighten out and help some of our really, truly great professional guys who really love you, and know how you really have the sympathy to want to help them. And I was just telling your story about Jonah Jones with he was in Cuba and he had a little trouble in Cuba because he drank the wrong kind of beer that paralyzed his chops and he got sick once and I know he came to you. What was that about?

Well, he didn't really come to me. I used to practice up in the studio, up next to his, and he'd come in there occasionally, up at Colin's Practice Studios. And one time I was teaching up there and I heard somebody in the next room, and I hear this huff, huff, for about an hour, and I thought maybe this was some new system. And I went in and asked Charlie, who's in there. And he said, 'Jonah Jones, he's lost his lip.' And I said, oh, my God, and I stuck my head in and said, hello, what happened?

He said, well, I got my teeth capped, because he used to grind his teeth and his teeth were down almost to the gums. And the dentist gave him these big, beautiful teeth, without taking into consideration he was a trumpet player, and Jonah

just couldn't get a sound. And he said he opened up in the Playboy Club in Chicago in 10 days and he didn't know what he was going to do. I said, it looks like you're going to have to stand around and smile a lot, because that's all you've got going, sort of kidding.

And then I said, you know, I have this sort of system, it was to help a kid that had braces on their teeth, and then I found out it was very good for developing a register and things, basically it's trying to develop a new embouchure because, you know, a person's been playing a certain length of time and they've got a lot of strength, they don't progress, obviously they don't have the right setting on their mouth, then. And I had discovered a way to get around what holds you back from developing. And I said, I think I can help you. He said, gee, that would be great. And I said, if you've only got 10 days, we'll have to get together everyday for the 10 days. Great. I said, well, as soon as this lesson's over -- so I sat there and I said, why did I open my big mouth, I don't know whether I can help him or not.
